subject: Borealis outage: 5xx/429 spike, retry storm impact + remediation & refund proposal
messages:
From: Sara Khan <sara.khan@borealiscloud.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@borealiscloud.com
Date: Fri, 31 Jul 2026 15:14:00 -0700
Subject: Severe 5xx/429 spike this morning — immediate assistance & credit request

Olga,

We experienced a sustained spike of 5xx and 429 responses across our production traffic between 09:02–09:51 UTC this morning. Our telemetry shows a retry storm from client-side retries amplified the errors and resulted in a 45% throughput degradation for our core customer-facing endpoints. This caused a cascade of delayed responses and a handful of timeouts in critical flows (billing webhook and auth).

Impact:
- ~12% of user requests failed with 5xx (spike, not transient).
- Widespread 429s as your front-end returned rate-limit responses under load.
- Several downstream retries pushed our worker queue depth beyond safe thresholds (we saw 30–60s processing delays).

We urgently need:
1) A clear root-cause summary and timeline.
2) A remediation timeline for mitigation steps (short + medium term).
3) A proposal for financial remediation / credit for the impacted window.

Attached: our service impact log (borealis-service-impact-log.xlsx) and a CSV with our request timeline.

This has been escalated to our PM and procurement teams. Please treat as high priority — we are briefing our execs this afternoon.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Khan
Platform Lead, Borealis Cloud
Attach: borealis-service-impact-log.xlsx, borealis-incident-timeline.csv

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 31 Jul 2026 15:47:22 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Severe 5xx/429 spike this morning — immediate assistance & credit request

Folks — forwarding Borealis escalation. Highlights: significant 5xx/429 spike + client retry amplification causing throughput collapse. They want root cause, mitigation timeline, and financial remediation.

Initial asks from me:
- Rishi: can you pull the serving runtime traces + kernel selection logs for the 09:00–10:00 UTC window (INF-2148)? I want to know whether a kernel fallback or padding caused increased latency.
- Marissa: draft a preliminary credit calc (per our SLA) and a short statement we can share with the customer today. Use conservative approach but leave room for negotiation.
- Hannah: please prepare an exec summary for our leadership (one-pager) — include customer impact, expected credits, and proposed communication cadence.

Attachments I'll include to customer later: internal incident timeline, proposed refund/credit PDF. For now, flagging this as P1.

Thanks — Olga
Olga Petrov
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 01 Aug 2026 02:12:08 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Severe 5xx/429 spike this morning — immediate assistance & credit request

On Fri, Jul 31, 2026 at 3:47 PM Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com> wrote:
> Folks — forwarding Borealis escalation.

Quick summary of findings from runtime traces (09:00–10:00 UTC):
- We observed a burst of requests with long prefix lengths that triggered dynamic kernel selection to switch to a slower attention kernel under heavy concurrency; this increased median latency by ~780ms for affected calls.
- The rate limiter policy at the edge began emitting 429s at 09:08 UTC when token-queue depth exceeded configured thresholds; rate limiter logic subsequently entered a protective backoff which caused client retries to queue up behind longer-running requests.
- KV cache invalidations were unusually frequent due to a model-hotpatch deployment at 08:45 UTC; the hotpatch caused transient cache churn, increasing cache miss rate.

Preliminary root cause (probable): model hotpatch + kernel fallback under high concurrency => elevated latencies -> edge rate limiting -> client retry amplification -> retry storm.

Immediate remediation performed (already done):
- Rolled back hotpatch at 09:25 UTC.
- Re-enabled a larger KV cache window and applied an interim kernel pin for the affected model variant.
- Throttled aggressive client retry headers via edge advisory rules.

Next steps (recommended):
1) Full postmortem with timeline and kernel telemetry (Jira INF-2148).
2) Revise model rollout gating to include kernel selection stability checks.
3) Add a short-circuit on the rate limiter to drop requests before queue explosion (soft-fail) and return structured error with TTL to clients.

I will attach the kernel logs and network trace (retry-storm-network-trace.pcap) to the ticket.

—Rishi

Attach: retry-storm-network-trace.pcap

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 01 Aug 2026 08:05:34 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Severe 5xx/429 spike this morning — immediate assistance & credit request

On Sat, Aug 1, 2026 at 2:12 AM Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com> wrote:
> Quick summary of findings from runtime traces...

Olga / team — here's a first-pass credit proposal based on our SLA (and taking into account their degree of impact and our rollback timing):
- Affected window: 09:02–09:51 UTC (49 minutes).
- SLA target: 99.95% (per contract). Observed error/429 rate during window equates to ~96.8% -- net unavailability ~3.15% for that window.
- Proposed credit: pro-rated refund for the impacted window = 3.15% * monthly committed spend. For negotiation, I recommend offering 5% of monthly committed spend as an initial good-faith offer plus one month of free Dedicated routing for their critical endpoints for 30 days (to reduce risk of recurrence).

Draft customer-facing language (short):
"We sincerely apologize for the disruption. Our investigation identified a model hotpatch that precipitated kernel fallbacks under heavy concurrency; we have rolled back the change, applied mitigations, and will provide a formal postmortem. As a gesture of goodwill we propose a credit equivalent to 5% of your monthly committed spend for the impacted period and 30 days of free Dedicated routing for affected endpoints. We are prepared to finalize this via standard commercial paperwork."

If we need exec sign-off for >5% or additional concessions let me know — otherwise I can send this to the customer with the postmortem ETA.

—Marissa

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Sara Khan <sara.khan@borealiscloud.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Severe 5xx/429 spike this morning — immediate assistance & credit request

Sara — thank you again for flagging this so quickly and for the impact data you sent. I appreciate the patience while our team completed their analysis.

Summary (short):
- What happened: a hotpatch to the model variant at ~08:45 UTC created an atypical pattern of prefix lengths and cache churn which caused our runtime to select a fallback kernel under heavy concurrency. That fallback increased per-request latency and triggered edge rate limiting; client retries amplified the load and produced a retry storm.
- Mitigation steps taken: rollback of hotpatch (09:25 UTC); expanded KV cache window; temporary kernel pin for the variant; short-term edge advisory to reduce client retries.
- Next steps: full postmortem (Jira INF-2148) due by EOD Tue 2026-08-03 with a permanent rollout gating proposal.

Customer remediation proposal (good-faith):
- A credit equal to 5% of your monthly committed spend applied to the upcoming invoice.
- 30 days of free Dedicated routing for the impacted endpoints to reduce recurrence risk.
- We will provide a signed amendment for accounting if you accept; DocuSign link below.

DocuSign (proposal): https://app.docusign.com/sign/XYZ-BOREALIS-INVITE
Attached: redwood-refund-proposal-v1.pdf (detailed calc), borealis-incident-timeline.csv, retry-storm-network-trace.pcap

Please let us know if the proposal is acceptable or if you prefer a call for faster alignment. We can also escalate to our commercial leadership if Borealis requires a different resolution path.

Best,
Olga
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
